newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: FORECAST-BCP seen posting higher H1 result.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-BCP seen posting higher H1 result.

text.p: A continued improvement in commissions and financial margins combined with lower costs have helped Portugal's largest private bank group, Banco Comercial Portugues (BCP), boost its first-half profit, analysts said.
Analysts expect BCP to announce consolidated net profit of between 13 and 13.5 billion escudos, up from around 11 billion in the same period last year.
They said that margins, commissions and costs had developed favourably in the first quarter and there were unlikely to have been any changes during the second.
BCP will present its results on July 22 after the share market closes.

"First-half profit should be around 13.2 billion thanks to an increase in commissions, which was linked to a better performance by (its unit) Banco Portugues do Atlantico BPA, lower costs, and an improvement in trading operations, although this was less dramatic than in the first quarter," said one analyst who declined to be named.
Increased cross-selling is also seen by analysts as a reason for BCP's good performance.
A Reuter survey of six analysts forecast that BCP would end the year with an annual net profit of between 26.5 and 28.5 billion escudos, compared with 23.3 billion escudos in 1996.
A London analyst said that BCP shares still had room to rise, due to good prospects for results and the possible sale by year's end of BCP's 20 percent stake in the insurer Mundial Confianca.
"The appetite for this stock takes account of the sale of the 20 percent BCP holds in Mundial Confianca, something which could happen this year," he said.
BCP's shares have also risen as earnings stemming from the acquisition of Banco Portugues do Atlantico have been entered in its accounts.
BCP's share price has gained more than 70 percent in 1997, having underperformed in 1996, to a high of 3,500 escudos reached on June 17th.
The stock was up 23 escudos at 3,433 on Thursday.
